As a non-American, I think the Reset with Russia was a good but short-lived start.

The problem was that the Russians saw the period of post-Bush foreign policy as a 1972-1973 Détente style, when the Americans had been weakened by the war in Vietnam and were on the defensive. The Russians have approached the reset believing that the United States were operating from a position of weakness given the two wars and the financial crisis.

The US approached Russia from a more open approach than its predecessor, George W. Bush. Obama had been actively seeking a more stable partnership with Putin's Russia. Obama genuinely thought that such a process was viable. The missile agreement was good for both Russia and the US, since both were trying to limit their ballistic weaponry COSTS. It also put Russia on a better position, ranking among world powers again. It joined the WTO one year later, in 2013.

The switch from Medvedev to Putin in 2012, however, inevitably led to a very authoritative and belligerant Russian foreign policy, which had even fewer areas of cooperation than before. The Reset died because it was misinterpreted by both sides, in the wake of the Libyan, Syrian and Ukrainian conflicts.

TL;DR Good initiative, misinterpreted by both sides, led to short-term progress but died because of very polarized disagreements.
